narrative.overview:
Leaf follows the owner's confirmed 简约风 direction: a light-first local LaTeX writing environment within the established compact neutral Operate world. Quiet writing surfaces, fine separators, small line icons and clear actions leave the document at the center. The approved Leaf name clarifies the product identity while retaining the incumbent layout, density, neutral palettes and optional assistant workflows.

The recurring identity is a genuine Lucide leaf outline beside the lowercase leaf wordmark and its terminal dot; compact library navigation uses l. and the local workspace avatar uses L. Fresh settings and the initial page use the existing light theme. A saved light, dark or system preference takes precedence; system follows the operating system rather than becoming a forced light choice. This is the current browser application; native packaging is deferred.

Leaf is the product name, while the existing Prism folder and prism_pro repository, data and integration namespaces remain compatible. Original Prism and Overleaf names still identify import sources, and the independent-software attribution retains its historical Prism reference. Existing assistant, API-provider and local CLI-login controls remain available. Earlier extension records below retain their original names and review boundaries; the identity amendment does not rewrite that historical evidence or certify the full Leaf plan.

The file-manager extension carries that character into upload, move, Trash and restore review. A centered dialog presents context, destination or affected paths, then a named action. Writing checks extends the same tool vocabulary with bundled English (US/UK) spelling, independent LaTeX hints and personal words: active-file context precedes inspectable findings and explicit corrections. Saved chats continue it through named conversation rows, a bounded reading area and compact source/review controls. Existing-table drafts extend the same vocabulary through a schematic source grid, native structure controls and review before one reversible Apply. Clipboard choices reuse that vocabulary through a captured target, native format choices, bounded content/source inspection and a reachable paste/recovery footer. Local comments continue it through the Review sidebar, original source quotes, rule-separated plain-text messages and reachable thread/reply controls. Ordinary source review extends that sidebar through complete removed/added passages, native selection and a reachable explicit decision. Project history continues this vocabulary through a flat timeline, read-only saved discussion/source disclosures and an explicit, bounded recovery plan. Milestone labels extend that history through restrained view/search controls, plain editable rows and recoverable removal beside the selected version. Local templates continue it through flat collections, inspectable frozen source, explicit separate PDF compilation and reachable create/capture actions. The project library continues it through named tag markers, archive navigation, native list/grid selection and exact-target reviews with reachable preparation, confirmation and recovery. Compile tools continue it through explicit next-build choices, immutable generated-file rows, strict read-only text and source/output ZIP review with persistent preparation/recovery controls. Local-first editing is the current product context; this document does not define the appearance of future hosted collaboration.

Persistent unsent chat prompts continue this vocabulary through compact local-save status, retained error text and a bounded comparison of literal window versions before an explicit choice.

Saved-chat search extends the same sidebar through literal title/prompt/reply excerpts, explicit archive restoration and exact saved-turn navigation while retaining each conversation's unsent prompt.

Installed-runtime choices extend the same vocabulary through a native selector, wrapping installation path, explicit unavailable-tool guidance and named refresh actions. Finished-build context keeps the resolved runtime beside the PDF, logs and generated files rather than presenting current settings as the identity of earlier output.

Diagnostic actions extend the same vocabulary through complete wrapping source labels, named inline preparation and recovery, and literal existing/proposed prompt review before Keep, Append or Replace. The actual source opens before composer review; Send remains a separate explicit action.

rules.name: The Neutral Actions Rule
rules.body: Keep primary operations neutral and inverted; use semantic color to explain state rather than recolor the entire review surface.

rules.name: The Saved Theme Rule
rules.body: Start fresh preferences in the existing light theme; preserve an explicit light, dark or system choice and resolve system through the operating system.

rules.name: The Compatible Identity Rule
rules.body: Name the current product Leaf while preserving original-source names, saved preferences, data and integration identifiers and existing assistant controls; a visible brand change does not authorize a namespace migration.

rules.name: The Review Before Apply Rule
rules.body: Put affected paths and the operation's current status before the final action; gate that action while a valid review is unavailable or an operation is running.

rules.name: The Explicit Correction Rule
rules.body: Keep the active-file context, finding and source excerpt ahead of a named correction; apply a source change only after the author chooses it, and keep it reversible through the editor's normal Undo.

rules.name: The Reachable History Rule
rules.body: Keep conversation identity and chronological paging outside the scrolling reply region, with the existing composer reachable below it; contain long code, math and tables within the reply.

rules.name: The Exact Saved Match Rule
rules.body: Keep the project/saved-message scope, literal excerpt and explicit archive restoration ahead of exact-turn navigation; retain one reachable Earlier/Newer/Return to latest group and preserve each conversation's unsent prompt without starting generation.

rules.name: The Confirmed Prompt Save Rule
rules.body: Keep exact unsent text with its project/conversation, distinguish pending text from a confirmed local save, and require an explicit choice between literal competing versions while retaining stale/error recovery; drafting never sends an AI request or changes source/history/session state.

rules.name: The Target-aware Preparation Rule
rules.body: Name and open the actual diagnostic source, preserve the conversation, scope and literal unsent prompt, reject stale preparation, and keep Keep/Append/Replace separate from explicit Send.

rules.name: The Named Typing Recovery Rule
rules.body: Keep the typing target, Retry and Dismiss explicit inside the bounded transcript; briefly lock mutations, save unrelated edits before restoring the target's source and selection, and distinguish preserved native history from reconstructed one-event Redo.

rules.name: The Source-preserving Draft Rule
rules.body: Keep table source and document history unchanged while the author selects, edits and reviews a local draft; show truthful logical selection, complete-source recovery and one explicit reversible Apply.

rules.name: The Reversible Clipboard Rule
rules.body: Paste ordinary supported content as one reversible edit; require review when source recovery, packages or detected losses need a choice, keeping the captured target, complete source and recovery action inspectable before insertion.

rules.name: The Reviewed Image Rule
rules.body: Review destination and replacement consent before saving a clipboard image, then insert its figure explicitly; keep upload recovery separate from document Undo.

rules.name: The Anchored Discussion Rule
rules.body: Keep original source context and changed/removed status truthful, preserve local wording across navigation or conflicts, and require an explicit retarget or saved-thread rebase before a stale draft is posted.

rules.name: The Reachable Thread Rule
rules.body: Keep thread return navigation and the end-of-thread reply reachable within the scrolling Review sidebar; retain read-only inspection and accessible source navigation while mutations are locked.

rules.name: The Exact Passage Review Rule
rules.body: Keep complete before/after source and coherent whole-passage selection ahead of an explicit revision-bound Accept/Reject confirmation; never silently accept pending work when Reviewing is turned off.

rules.name: The Reachable Decision Rule
rules.body: Keep confirmation, Cancel and complete source inspection reachable inside the scrolling Changes sidebar, with keyboard source access and truthful read-only/stale gating.

rules.name: The Explicit Recovery Scope Rule
rules.body: Keep the selected version, exact file/project scope, review inclusion and newer-discussion fate visible before Confirm restore; retain current chats and Editing/Reviewing mode.

rules.name: The Reachable Recovery Rule
rules.body: Keep history identity, saved content and confirmation errors inspectable in bounded regions, with keyboard focus and Confirm/Cancel reachable in both themes.

rules.name: The Stable Version Context Rule
rules.body: Filter active names without changing the selected saved version; keep its saved date, full label list and an explicit Show all history recovery available.

rules.name: The Recoverable Label Rule
rules.body: Keep label mutation separate from saved content, preserve local wording across stale or ambiguous responses, and provide explicit Refresh, replay-safe Retry and Removed labels recovery.

rules.name: The Inspected Snapshot Rule
rules.body: Keep local template provenance, frozen source and explicit separate compilation ahead of creation; distinguish metadata changes and recoverable Trash from the source copied into a fresh project.

rules.name: The Reachable Capture Rule
rules.body: Keep included source and retained error/retry context inspectable in the scrolling body while the dialog heading and explicit Save/Cancel remain reachable outside it.

rules.name: The Exact Library Targets Rule
rules.body: Keep captured project identities visible before and after preflight, and require a current exact-target review before applying a batch; a busy member blocks the whole Trash action with named no-mutation and Refresh recovery context.

rules.name: The Truthful Download Review Rule
rules.body: Keep prepared and requested states distinct, preserve exact targets and recovery actions after link activation, and never promote a browser request into a saved-file claim.

rules.name: The Captured Build Choices Rule
rules.body: Keep next-build options separate from immutable finished-build context; label draft and erroneous output explicitly and preserve last-successful recovery.

rules.name: The Explicit Runtime Rule
rules.body: Keep System versus a pinned installation, availability and recovery visible before saving; identify finished output by its captured runtime and never silently substitute an engine or installation.

rules.name: The Retained Build Selection Rule
rules.body: Keep search, selection actions and count outside the generated-row scroller, with build identity and Review ZIP reachable while literal file text is inspected.

rules.name: The Archive-only Replacement Rule
rules.body: Name every differing source/output path and require explicit consent before preparing replacement bytes inside a ZIP; keep the immutable build, review and recovery controls visible after preparation and request.

rules.name: The Retained Preview Rule
rules.body: Keep the replacement, named build/status and explicit Stop/Retry inside the bounded review, with heading and approval/recovery actions reachable while the body scrolls; require an explicit Start typing after compiler drain.

rules.name: The Truthful Preview Result Rule
rules.body: Acknowledge confirmed cancellation even before a job exists, and describe an earlier preview result without claiming a PDF that the build did not produce.

donts: **Don't** introduce a replacement visual identity or decorative accent palette in a local file-manager, writing-tool, chat or table extension.
**Don't** turn ordinary review rows into competing raised cards.
**Don't** replace path/status text or native controls with icon-only explanations.
**Don't** multiply the shell's tiny tracked metadata into a new heading or component system.
**Don't** treat narrow dialog captures as proof of a responsive mobile editor or future collaboration design.
**Don't** treat narrow chat-pane containment or still captures as full-editor mobile, transient-state or motion certification.
**Don't** silently merge or overwrite competing prompts, close comparison before a chosen save is confirmed or create a chat/session/source/history change from drafting alone.
**Don't** promise abrupt-crash durability before a prompt save commits, treat a restored draft as saved model/source context or infer live-provider/full-parity certification from synthetic checks.
**Don't** present the schematic table grid or width controls as a typeset preview, or conceal source-only boundaries.
**Don't** treat the table fix verdict, contained narrow dialog or functional checks as whole-surface, mobile-editor or motion certification.
**Don't** imply arbitrary HTML/CSS fidelity, automatically add/install packages or fetch remote clipboard images.
**Don't** treat the clipboard's two-fix ship verdict, still captures or narrow containment as whole-app, mobile-editor, contrast or motion certification.
**Don't** silently overwrite a local comment draft, treat escaped messages as Markdown or place hidden gutter buttons in the tab order.
**Don't** imply that unsent comment drafts survive restart, local You-only comments provide hosted discussion or ordinary tracked changes, or narrow comments captures establish a mobile editor.
**Don't** treat the comments SHIP verdict as visual certification of uncaptured lists, Trash, focused states, motion, computed contrast or unsampled backend branches.
**Don't** silently accept pending changes when tracking is disabled, fragment coherent passages into repeated deletion widgets or hide complete removed source.
**Don't** conflate source Undo with review-decision Undo or imply local You-only source review supplies hosted coauthor permissions or notifications.

**Don't** describe comments or pending baselines as excluded from history by default, roll current chats/mode back with a version or imply source ZIP exports carry review metadata.

**Don't** discard a retained label draft on refresh, conflate recoverable removal with deleting a version, or imply open-dialog drafts survive restart.
